dublinCore.title: Convolution Theorem and Circular Convolution
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Convolution theorem
Circular convolution
Linear convolution
Discrete Fourier transform
Zero padding
Time aliasing
dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim that compares the linear convolution of two short sequences (length N + M - 1) with their L-point circular convolution, computed both by wrapping the linear result onto itself and by the DFT route IDFT_L(DFT_L(x) DFT_L(h)). When L < N + M - 1 the wrapped samples are drawn in red with arrows to where they land, an error panel shows the difference, and the magnitude spectra |X[k]|, |H[k]| and |Y[k]| = |X[k]||H[k]| can be read bin by bin.

learningObjectives: Calculate the length N + M - 1 of a linear convolution and the smallest DFT length L for which IDFT_L{X[k]H[k]} equals it
Explain circular convolution as linear convolution with its tail wrapped around, y_c[n] = sum_m y[n + mL], and identify the time-aliased samples when L < N + M - 1
Verify the convolution theorem Y[k] = X[k]H[k] by comparing the DFT route with the wrap-around sum and by reading |X[k]|, |H[k]| and |Y[k]| at one bin
Evaluate whether a transform length L is adequate for a given pair of sequences, including cases where the wrapped samples happen to be zero
Predict that a delay becomes a circular shift (rotation) when L is too short
prerequisites: Definition of the DFT and its inverse

misconceptions.misconception: Multiplying two FFTs gives the (linear) convolution
misconceptions.correction: The product of two L-point DFTs is the DFT of the circular convolution; it equals the linear convolution only when L >= N + M - 1
misconceptions.evidence: With the defaults (triangle N = 8, rectangle M = 4, L = 8) the gold IDFT rings agree with the wrap-around sum to about 1e-15, yet the error panel shows a maximum error of 6 against the linear result

misconceptions.misconception: Extra zero padding changes the convolution result
misconceptions.correction: Any L >= N + M - 1 gives the same linear result followed by zeros; extra padding only samples the spectrum more finely
misconceptions.evidence: With the defaults, L = 11, 16 and 64 all show the same 11 samples and a maximum error of 0

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Five stacked stem plots compare linear and circular convolution. Top: the input x[n] and the impulse response h[n]. Second: the linear convolution y[n] of length N + M - 1. Third: the L-point circular convolution, with gold rings showing the result of the DFT route IDFT(DFT(x) times DFT(h)). When L is shorter than N + M - 1 the samples of y beyond L are drawn in red and arrows show where they wrap around. Fourth: the error between circular and linear convolution. Bottom: the DFT magnitudes |X[k]|, |H[k]| and |Y[k]|. Drop-down lists and sliders choose the two sequences, their lengths N and M, and the transform length L.

visualElements.description: Stem plots of x[n] (blue) and h[n] (purple) on n = 0..15
Linear convolution y[n] (green), with the samples at n >= L shaded and drawn in red
Red arrows from each wrapped sample of y[n] to the circular sample n mod L where it lands
L-point circular convolution y_c[n] (teal, time-aliased samples red, labelled with their sums) with gold rings for IDFT_L(X[k]H[k])
Error e[n] = y_c[n] - y[n] (red) with its maximum
Scaled magnitude spectra |X[k]|, |H[k]| and |Y[k]|; hovering a bin prints its three magnitudes
Required length N + M - 1, chosen L, number of wrapped samples, maximum error and whether circular equals linear

model.description: Computes the linear convolution y[n], the L-point circular convolution by periodic summation y_c[n] = sum_m y[n + mL], and the DFT route IDFT_L(DFT_L(x) DFT_L(h)) with a naive O(L^2) DFT; the error is y_c[n] - y[n] with each sequence zero outside its own length
equations: y[n] = sum_k x[k] h[n - k], length N + M - 1
y_c[n] = sum_m y[n + mL], 0 <= n < L
y_c = y (zero-padded) if L >= N + M - 1
algorithms: Naive DFT and inverse DFT, O(L^2)

instructionalStrategies: Predict the wrapped samples before reading the labels
Increase L one step at a time until the error vanishes
Read |X[k]|, |H[k]| and |Y[k]| at one bin to confirm the product
extensions: Add the phase spectra to show that a delayed impulse changes only phase
Add an overlap-add mode that filters a long signal block by block
